source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Reduced patient involvement in their own care overall, contrary to the actual goal and effect of this newer bedside reporting approach","B":"Decreased accuracy of information transfer between shifts, contrary to the improved accuracy this approach is actually intended to support","C":"No meaningful difference from station-based reporting, contrary to the specific benefits this bedside approach is actually designed to provide","D":"Increased engagement, since both nurses assess the client together with the client present, rather than the objectifying experience the veteran nurse is worried about"}}
source_row.rationale: Bedside shift report, with the client present when appropriate and desired, is associated with increased patient engagement (allowing the client to participate in and help verify shared information) and improved safety, since both the outgoing and incoming nurses can visually assess the client together at the start of the shift, potentially catching issues (such as a change in a dressing or IV site) that might otherwise be missed.
source_row.source_detail: Benefits of Bedside vs. Station-Based Shift Report
source_row.source_name: AHRQ — Bedside Shift Report Implementation Guide
source_row.stem: A hospital transitions from conducting shift-to-shift report exclusively at the nurses' station to conducting bedside shift report, with the client present when possible, though a veteran nurse worries this change will actually make the client feel like just an object being discussed.
